audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor History at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies global historical change and uses historical and social-science methods to investigate contemporary questions. Students choose a focus area and complete an individual History thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines historical inquiry with economic and social explanation. The second focuses on international relations, conflict and institutions; the third on social and cultural history. Each includes all six UCR History courses, with historical source analysis and a substantial research paper. Economics, law, rhetoric and other fields support the historical questions while retaining their own methods. Shared rows show partial curricular relationships; blank cells preserve substantive gaps.

curriculum.routeLabel: Economic History; minor and selected internship
curriculum.limitation: One permitted 2026–2027 pathway is shown. Other focus areas and the approved elective, exchange and educational-minor routes remain available.

componentNotes.y2-elective: One 7.5-EC course selected from the programme’s permitted elective options.
componentNotes.y3-thesis-class: Thesis class in the Economic History focus area. Entry requires completed Year 1 and 45 EC in Years 2–3, including 22.5 EC in the focus area (three courses).
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Individually assessed historical research within the selected focus-area thesis class. The class must be completed before submission. A timely submitted thesis has a resit under the TER; the resit grade is capped at 6.0.
componentNotes.y3-minor: One 15-EC minor from the admission matrix, with its admission requirements; participation requires at least third-year enrolment. The selected route does not combine this with the alternative exchange or educational-minor route.
componentNotes.y3-internship: Selected 15-EC field-specific placement, replaceable by two permitted electives. Entry requires all BA1 courses passed. Normally in the second term of Year 3 for History; another term may be requested. Approved placement concludes within six consecutive months and is graded pass/fail.
componentNotes.y1-global: The current pathway follows the 2026–2027 regulations. Exams in Years 2–3 normally require positive binding study advice; the first-year standard is 60 EC, subject to the regulations’ compensation and personal-circumstances provisions. Practicals are compulsory: the published absence limit is three in first-year History and two thereafter, with missed assignments still due.
